If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
For mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment swings from positive to negative, shift forecast downward by 1–2% in the 3rd–5th day of the forecast window.  
For late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, apply a downward correction of 2–3% to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the last 5 days to dampen momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the last 5 days to prevent premature collapse.
